title: Validate the dossier and export the eCTD package
walkthrough:
You start on the dossier manager page, under a top bar branded "ANDS Studio". The heading reads "Your product dossiers", and each dossier is a tile showing its ID, product name, a progress bar, and a chip reading either "Ready to file" or a count like "3/5 modules". You click a tile to open the dossier; it lands you in the Module 1 workspace.

The workspace has three columns: a section tree on the left, the selected section's panel in the middle, and a right-hand rail of cards. The top bar shows module tabs "M1" through "M5" (each with a ✓, — or ● state dot) plus chips for "Application Viewer", "Audit", "Portfolio" and "Journey".

Validation lives in the right rail. A module card shows a progress bar, a line like "12/15 required sections complete", and three readiness flags: "Documents", "Fee", and "Valid eCTD", each marked ✓ or ○. If the filing gate is not complete, a note says how many "item(s) still needed to file (documents, fee, or validation).".

Below that sits the "eCTD validation" card. It always displays the structural check result as a status badge — "● PASSED" in green, or a red count like "● 3 error(s)" with up to five bulleted error messages beneath, plus a line such as "2 warning(s)". To run the deeper technical check, you click "Run full check (PDF conformance)"; the button reads "Checking…" while it runs, then the badge and error list update with the full result.

Exporting happens in the "Sequences" card just above. It lists each eCTD sequence by its four-digit number (e.g. 0000), a purpose chip ("Response", "Supplement", "Annual notification" or "Initial"), a leaf count like "3 leaf(s)", and either an "● ACTIVE" marker or a "Make active" button. The card header shows "working: 0000" — the sequence new documents land in. Each row has an "Export" link that directly downloads that sequence's eCTD package; there is no confirmation step or progress indicator, and nothing blocks export if validation has not passed. Clicking "New sequence" opens an inline form: the next number is auto-assigned (shown as "New sequence 0001"), you pick a purpose from a dropdown, optionally type a note (placeholder: "Note (e.g. screening deficiency SDN-1)"), and click "Create & make active" or "Cancel".

Note: creating a dossier in the first place requires knowing the ID format — the form rejects anything but one letter plus 6–7 digits, with the error "Dossier ID must be one letter + 6–7 digits (e.g. e123456)".
